CRA-MFG_1.title: Product Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
CRA-MFG_1.description: Perform a cybersecurity risk assessment for the product with digital elements (CRA Art. 13(2)).

CRA-MFG_2.title: Manufacturer Due Diligence
CRA-MFG_2.description: Exercise due diligence when integrating components from third parties, free and open-source ones included, so that they do not compromise the product's cybersecurity (CRA Art. 13(5)). The CRA asks for no signature here; in this product management confirms it.

CRA-ESS_1.title: Secure-by-Design Requirements
CRA-ESS_1.description: Design and produce products to meet the essential cybersecurity requirements (CRA Annex I Part I).

CRA-ESS_2.title: Secure Default Configuration
CRA-ESS_2.description: Make products available with a secure-by-default configuration (Annex I Part I, point 2(b)).

CRA-ESS_3.title: No Known Exploitable Vulnerabilities
CRA-ESS_3.description: Make products available on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities (Annex I Part I, point 2(a)).

CRA-VLN_1.title: Vulnerability Handling Policy
CRA-VLN_1.description: Establish a process to identify, document and remediate vulnerabilities (CRA Annex I Part II, points 1 to 2).

CRA-VLN_2.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
CRA-VLN_2.description: Put in place and enforce a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy (Annex I Part II, point 5) and provide a contact address for reporting vulnerabilities (point 6).

CRA-VLN_3.title: Security Update Delivery
CRA-VLN_3.description: Remediate vulnerabilities without delay through security updates, distribute them securely, and disseminate available updates without delay and free of charge, with advisory messages for users (Annex I Part II, points 2, 7 and 8).

CRA-VLN_4.title: Vulnerability Testing
CRA-VLN_4.description: Apply effective and regular tests and reviews of the product's security (Annex I Part II, point 3).

CRA-INC_1.title: Early Warning Notification
CRA-INC_1.description: Send an early warning of an actively exploited vulnerability to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and ENISA without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of it (CRA Art. 14(2)(a)).

CRA-INC_2.title: Vulnerability Notification
CRA-INC_2.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability, submit the vulnerability notification to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and to ENISA, unless that information has already been provided (CRA Art. 14(2)(b)).

CRA-INC_3.title: Final Vulnerability Report
CRA-INC_3.description: No later than 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available, submit the final report on the actively exploited vulnerability: its description, severity and impact, any malicious actor exploiting it, and the security update (CRA Art. 14(2)(c)).

CRA-INC_4.title: User Notification
CRA-INC_4.description: Inform the impacted users, and where appropriate all users, of an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident and, where necessary, of the mitigation and corrective measures they can take (CRA Art. 14(8)).

CRA-CONF_1.title: Conformity Assessment
CRA-CONF_1.description: Carry out the conformity assessment of the product and of your own processes against the essential cybersecurity requirements of Annex I (CRA Art. 32(1)).

CRA-CONF_2.title: CE Marking and Conformity
CRA-CONF_2.description: Draw up the EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking (CRA Art. 28, Art. 30).

CRA-DOC_1.title: CRA Technical Documentation
CRA-DOC_1.description: Draw up the technical documentation, with at least the elements of Annex VII, before placing the product on the market, and keep it updated at least during the support period (CRA Art. 31).

CRA-SUP_1.title: Support Period
CRA-SUP_1.description: Determine the support period so that it reflects how long the product is expected to be in use, and record what you took into account in the technical documentation (CRA Art. 13(8)). It is at least five years, unless the product is expected to be in use for less. The CRA asks for no signature; in this product management signs it off.

CRA-SBOM_1.title: Software Bill of Materials
CRA-SBOM_1.description: Produce a software bill of materials covering the top-level dependencies (CRA Annex I Part II, point 1).

CRA-IMP_1.title: Importer Obligations
CRA-IMP_1.description: As an importer, place on the market only products that meet the essential cybersecurity requirements, after checking the manufacturer's conformity assessment, technical documentation, CE marking and declaration of conformity (CRA Art. 19).

CRA-IMP_2.title: Distributor Obligations
CRA-IMP_2.description: As a distributor, act with due care, check the CE marking and the manufacturer's and importer's documents before making a product available, and hold back products you believe do not conform (CRA Art. 20).

CRA-OSS_1.title: Open-Source Steward Duties
CRA-OSS_1.description: Document the cybersecurity policy expected of open-source software stewards (CRA Art. 24).
